name: SDF Primitive Definitions
text:
# SDF Primitive Definitions


## Overview
[SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md) Primitive Definitions provide closed-form analytical functions for canonical 3D shapes (spheres, boxes, tori, planes) that serve as the foundational building blocks for procedural geometry in [distance-field ray marching](#21-distance-field-ray-marching.md) [G]. They solve the problem of defining scene geometry without explicit mesh tessellation by providing conservative distance estimates that guarantee ray step sizes will not overshoot surfaces [G]. Unlike [Constructive SDF Modeling (Min Combination)](871-constructive-sdf-modeling-min-combination.md) which combines primitives, this method focuses on the base analytical definitions of canonical shapes and their immediate geometric properties [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Signed Distance Field Representations and Operations](13339-signed-distance-field-representations-and-operations.md).

## Subtopics

### [Constructive SDF Modeling (Min Combination)](871-constructive-sdf-modeling-min-combination.md)
[Constructive SDF Modeling (Min Combination)](#871-constructive-sdf-modeling-min-combination.md) computes the signed distance from a query point to the geometric union of multiple primitives by returning the minimum of their individual signed distance functions (SDFs) [G]. It solves the problem of representing complex scenes composed of many objects as a single continuous distance field, enabling efficient [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) by ensuring the returned distance is a conservative lower bound to the nearest surface [G]. What sets it apart from its siblings, such as [Smooth SDF Composition](2685-smooth-sdf-composition.md), is that it produces sharp, non-differentiable boundaries at intersections rather than smooth transitions, and it differs from [Boolean Operations on Distance Fields](1961-boolean-operations-on-distance-fields.md) by specifically implementing the union operation via the `min` operator, whereas intersection and difference require `max` or negation [G]. See [Constructive SDF Modeling (Min Combination)](871-constructive-sdf-modeling-min-combination.md).

### [Pyroclastic Sphere Primitive](1579-pyroclastic-sphere-primitive.md)
The [Pyroclastic Sphere Primitive](#1579-pyroclastic-sphere-primitive.md) is a procedural signed distance field (SDF) primitive that displaces a base sphere's surface using procedural noise to create organic, turbulent shapes with overhangs [G]. It distinguishes itself from static SDF primitives by combining a low-frequency sinusoidal "breathing" modulation with high-frequency [fractal Brownian motion](#22237-fractal-brownian-motion.md) (fBM) and sinusoidal products to generate complex surface topology [G]. Unlike standard sphere primitives, it supports 2D displacement to prevent density disconnection, making it suitable for volumetric effects like smoke or lava [G]. See [Pyroclastic Sphere Primitive](1579-pyroclastic-sphere-primitive.md).

### [Offset Surface Evaluation](1782-offset-surface-evaluation.md)
[Offset Surface Evaluation](#1782-offset-surface-evaluation.md) computes the signed distance from a query point to a surface generated by offsetting a base "skeleton" geometry by a fixed distance [G]. It solves the problem of defining smooth, thickened representations of curves, surfaces, or meshes for use in implicit modeling and ray marching [G]. It is distinguished from its siblings by its reliance on a global point-to-set distance search (global offset) rather than a local parametric displacement, which avoids the interior self-intersections and high-degree algebraic artifacts common in local offset methods [G]. See [Offset Surface Evaluation](1782-offset-surface-evaluation.md).

### [Boolean Operations on Distance Fields](1961-boolean-operations-on-distance-fields.md)
Boolean operations on Signed Distance Fields (SDFs) are Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) primitives that combine two or more base SDFs to create complex shapes by performing set-theoretic unions, intersections, and differences [G]. Unlike standard geometric primitives, these operations allow the construction of arbitrary topology from simple building blocks without requiring mesh generation [G]. The method is distinguished by its reliance on component-wise minimum and maximum functions to preserve the distance field property, ensuring that the resulting function remains a valid [distance field for ray marching](#9643-sphere-tracing-and-step-rules.md) [G]. See [Boolean Operations on Distance Fields](1961-boolean-operations-on-distance-fields.md).

### [Standard Solid Primitives](16223-standard-solid-primitives.md)
[Standard Solid Primitives](#16223-standard-solid-primitives.md) are closed-form analytical Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) for canonical 3D shapes, serving as the foundational building blocks for procedural geometry in distance-field ray marching [G]. They solve the problem of defining scene geometry without explicit mesh tessellation by providing conservative distance estimates that guarantee ray step sizes will not overshoot surfaces [G]. Unlike [Constructive SDF Modeling (Min Combination)](871-constructive-sdf-modeling-min-combination.md) which combines primitives, this method focuses on the base analytical definitions of canonical shapes (spheres, boxes, tori, etc.) and their immediate geometric properties [G]. See [Standard Solid Primitives](16223-standard-solid-primitives.md).

### [Implicit Surface Representation](7277-implicit-surface-representation.md)
#### definition
Representation of an implicit surface as a grid-based Signed Distance Function (SDF) using [tricubic interpolation](#14963-tricubic-interpolation.md) to ensure continuous surface normals [G].
#### usage
Not given in the sources.

### SDF Bounding Box Clipping
#### definition
A technique to restrict a signed distance field (SDF) to a specific bounding box by intersecting the object's SDF with a [box SDF](#1332-box-sdf.md), avoiding artifacts caused by [clamping](#11530-clamping.md) coordinates [S1, unofficial].
#### step
Compute the object's local SDF value (`d_pt`) using the modulo-repeated coordinate pattern [S1, unofficial]. Calculate the bounding box extents and center: `bb_extents = (bounding_box_max - bounding_box_min) * 0.5` and `bb_center = bounding_box_min + bb_extents` [S1, unofficial]. Compute the distance from the point to the box surface: `bb_p = max(abs(p - bb_center) - bb_extents, 0.)` [S1, unofficial]. Compute the box SDF as the maximum component of `bb_p`: `d_bb = max(max(bb_p.x, bb_p.y), bb_p.z)` [S1, unofficial]. Return the maximum of the object SDF and the box SDF to intersect them: `return max(d_pt, d_bb)` [S1, unofficial].
#### pitfall
Clamping coordinates (e.g., `clamp(p.xyz, min, max)`) before computing the SDF results in the SDF returning a constant distance very close to the surface, causing raymarching to run out of iterations and produce stretched artifacts [S1, unofficial].

### SDF Scene Graph API
#### definition
A fluent API for defining 3D scenes using Signed Distance Field (SDF) primitives, boolean/smooth operators, and transformations, tagged with hatch directions [S2, unofficial].
#### step
Create primitives: `SdfNode.sphere(center, radius)`, `SdfNode.box_(size)`, `SdfNode.torus(major_radius, minor_radius)`, `SdfNode.plane_y(y_value)` [S2, unofficial]. Apply transformations: `.displace(freq, amp)`, `.round(radius)`, `.rotate_x/y/z(angle)`, `.translate((x, y, z))`, `.repeat_xz()` [S2, unofficial]. Combine nodes: `.smooth_union(other_node, k)`, `.smooth_subtract(other_node, k)`, `.union(other_node)`, `.intersect(other_node)`, `.subtract(other_node)`, where `k` is the blending radius for smooth variants [S2, unofficial]. Set hatch direction: `.hatch_dir(x, y, z)` sets the 3D tangent vector that strokes follow on that subtree's surface [S2, unofficial].
